examples: This dictionary shows the phonetics of the words.
wiktionary.gloss: The study of the physical sounds of human speech, concerned with the physical properties of speech sounds (phones), and the processes of their physiological production, auditory reception, and neurophysiological perception, and their representation by written symbols.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English, borrowed from Medieval Latin pleura.

thesaurus.definition: the thin serous membrane around the lungs and inner walls of the chest

translations.header: serous membrane that covers the lungs and thorax

examples: The lungs […] may be said to be inclosed in separate bags, or to have distinct pleuras.
wiktionary.gloss: Each of a pair of smooth serous membranes which line the thorax and envelop the lungs in humans and other mammals.
A lateral part in an animal body or structure.

blocks.etymology: From possible + -ly.

senses.definition: used to say that something may happen or might be true, but is not certain

examples.en: She will possibly arrive late because of heavy traffic.
examples.vi: Có lẽ cô ấy sẽ đến muộn vì tắc đường.

senses.definition: used with can or could to emphasize whether an action can be done at all

examples.en: I cannot possibly finish this report before tonight.
examples.vi: Tôi không thể nào hoàn thành báo cáo này trước tối nay.

thesaurus.definition: by chance

examples: Near-synonyms: maybe, perhaps, mayhap, mayhaps, by chance, perchance, peradventure; conceivably
Possibly, they will make gains in the midterm elections.
wiktionary.gloss: Perhaps; indicates that the proposition may be true (is not certainly false) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker.

examples: I'm much stronger than you, so you can't possibly win.
I couldn't possibly be there on time.
wiktionary.gloss: In the realm of possibility; indicates that the action may successfully be performed (is not impossible) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker that might limit the performance.

tatoeba.en: Possibly the factory will be closed down next week.
tatoeba.vi: Có lẽ tuần sau công ty sẽ đóng cửa.

tatoeba.en: Tom might possibly say something we don't want to hear.
tatoeba.vi: Tom có thể nói ra một điều gì đó mà chúng ta không muốn nghe.

examples: I like to relax pottering about the house doing this and that at the weekends.
wiktionary.gloss: To potter, to be gently active doing various things in an almost aimless manner.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English primer, primere, from Medieval Latin primarius and primarium (“prayer book”) possibly via Anglo-Norman primer (“prayer book”), from prima (“prime the liturgical hour and office”) + -arius and -arium (suffix forming related objects). Its use for schoolbooks derived from the late medieval and early modern use of such prayer books to teach reading.

senses.definition: a special paint or substance put on a surface before painting to help the paint stick

examples.en: Apply a coat of primer before painting the wooden door.
examples.vi: Hãy sơn một lớp sơn lót trước khi sơn cánh cửa gỗ.

senses.definition: a simple book or guide that introduces a subject or teaches beginners how to read

examples.en: The booklet is a useful primer for anyone investing in the stock market.
examples.vi: Cuốn sách nhỏ này là một tài liệu cơ bản hữu ích cho bất kỳ ai đầu tư chứng khoán.

senses.vi: sách vỡ lòng; tài liệu cơ bản

senses.definition: a cosmetic cream or gel applied to the skin before foundation to create a smooth surface

examples.en: She always uses a primer to keep her makeup fresh all day.
examples.vi: Cô ấy luôn dùng kem lót để giữ lớp trang điểm tươi tắn cả ngày.

senses.definition: a small device or substance used to ignite gunpowder or make a bomb explode

blocks.etymology: From Middle English swath, swathe, from Old English swæþ, swaþu (“track; trace; footstep”), from Proto-Germanic *swaþō (“a wind-swept place; open field”), of unknown further origin. Has been derived from a Proto-Indo-European *swey- (“to bend, turn, swing”), and compared with Ancient Greek σιμός (simós, “snub-nosed”) and Welsh chwil (“reeling, staggering”), though this is uncertain, as well as the Greek comparandum being unlikely. Cognate with Dutch zwade, zwad (“swath; windrow”), German Schwade (“swath; windrow”), Icelandic svæði (“area; zone; sector; region”).

senses.definition: a long wide strip of land, or a large part of a group of people.

examples.en: The storm destroyed a wide swath of forest.
examples.vi: Cơn bão đã tàn phá một vệt rừng rộng lớn.

examples.en: The new tax policy affects a large swath of voters.

idioms.gloss: To clear a broad track through a grassland, woodland, geographical region, or other area, either by natural means or by human action.
